title: Potential duality preserves bounded constructibility before biduality
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $r\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$, and $X$ a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $\delta$ be a dimension function and $K$ a pinned potential dualizing complex for $(X,\delta,\Lambda)$ [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Then for every $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the complex $D_KM=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. This assertion assumes no invertibility of any evaluation biduality map.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 6.2.3.1, printed pp.295–296 (preservation, preceding the biduality theorem)
